LESSON: READING 2.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: SHORT STORY (CLASS READER)

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.4: Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story (Class Reader)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story (Class Reader), part of Strand 2 in Grade 8 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Which places in the short stories would you like to visit? 2. Which time in history would you desire to live?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. watch different places and times of the day and night from a digital device or written text,

2. read a short story and retell

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. watch different places and times of the day and night from a digital device or written text,
2. read a short story and retell

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story (Class Reader) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital literacy: It is enhanced as the learner manipulates digital devices while looking at different places at different times.

• Imagination and creativity: These are brought out as the learner undertakes tasks that encourage artistic expression while

drawing or taking pictures of different settings.

Values:
Unity: It is fostered as the learner displays team spirit while working with peers to compare the setting in the short story with

that of their environment.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Peace education: It is enhanced as the learner appreciates the fact that different people live in different places.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the content of short stories to similar content in other subjects such as Religious Education.
